description: baseline

Batch-parallel BLOCKED Householder QR in Triton, attacking the trailing-update GEMM throughput that geqrf's 90%-unblocked-panel kernel wastes. Custom Triton kernel factors each width-~32-64 column panel across all batched matrices (compute V below-diag + tau + R on-diag), then apply the blocked update A -= V @ (T @ (V^T @ A)) as batched bf16/tf32 tensor-core GEMMs (torch.bmm or Triton) with fp32 accumulation. fp32-correct first, then bf16 trailing for the bulk. Output compact (H,tau); route off-grid n to torch.geqrf. Target dominant B=640 n=512.

Blocked Householder QR: Triton panel kernel (width-32 panel, one launch/all matrices, SRAM-resident per-column reflectors -> compact H,tau) + fp32 bmm trailing update A-=V@(T^T@(V^T@A)). Off-grid n -> geqrf. Validates clean incl all 3 guards. Profile: 33% elementwise (the sub_ + form_T loop launches), 17%+15% fp32 GEMMs, 12% panel kernel, 7% tiny form_T launches. Next: fuse sub into baddbmm, tf32/bf16 GEMMs, vectorize form_T.

Fused baddbmm trailing update + closed-form T (triu(V^T V,1)+diag(1/tau)) via solve_triangular, eliminating thousands of tiny form_T launches and the big elementwise sub_. tf32 reverted (fails ill-conditioned large-n gates). geomean 8038 us = 3.1x vs prev, 14.6x vs baseline.

bf16x3 split GEMM (fp32-accuracy via Ah@Bh+Ah@Bl+Al@Bh, fp32 accum/out, fused beta/alpha epilogue) replacing fp32 bmm in trailing update. Deterministic block heuristic (autotune corrupts in-place buffer + explodes validate time). Validates clean incl all guards. geomean 8313 = slight regression vs 8038; bf16x3 only wins when M,N,K all large but QR GEMMs are skinny (K=32). Next: apply bf16x3 selectively by shape; widen panels.

Per-n panel width (R={32:32,176:32,352:64,512:64,1024:32,2048:16,4096:16}) + reverted trailing update to fp32 bmm. Panel kernel holds full (m-j)xR panel in SRAM so narrow R essential at large n. Validates clean incl all guards. geomean 6702 = 1.20x vs prev, 17.5x vs baseline. n=2048 86->27ms, n=4096 462->202ms. Next: panel kernel still dominates large n (does not scale in m); needs a tall-skinny/recursive panel scheme.

geqrf-panel (R=128) for n=4096 where tiny batch (B=2) starves the one-CTA-per-matrix Triton panel; cuSOLVER geqrf spreads the tall-skinny panel over many CTAs. Other n keep Triton panel + fp32 bmm trailing. Validates clean incl all guards. geomean 5974 = 1.12x vs prev, 19.7x vs baseline. n=4096 202->53ms. Next: profile n=512 (4 shapes, dominant geomean weight).

Per-shape trailing precision: bf16x3 split GEMM trailing for n=2048/4096 (large GEMMs amortize 3 tensor-core passes; fp32 bmm kept for n<=1024 where GEMMs are skinny), geqrf panel R=256 for n=4096. bf16x3 passes gates incl n=4096 upper + diff guard. geomean 5878 = 1.02x vs prev, 20.0x vs baseline. n=2048 27.6->26.2ms, n=4096 53.6->50ms.

Cleanup: removed dead _SUPPORTED_N/_PANEL_R (config dict is sole source). No functional change. geomean 5928 (within noise of 5878, 20x baseline). Final n=512 profile: panel kernel 46.1% (THE bottleneck, capped by 100KB sm_120 SRAM wall + sequential BLAS-2 columns), trailing GEMMs 42% (magma V^T@A 27.9% + cutlass V@W 13.9%), trsm/form_T 4.7%, triu_tril 2.7%. Validates clean incl all guards.

BLOCKED Householder QR (Triton panel + blocked trailing GEMM) reached geomean 5878 us = 20.0x over the 117536 baseline (best commit dc5a3df6, all 22 tests + 3 guards clean). Path: blocked structure + Triton panel kernel (one CTA/matrix, panel resident in SRAM, per-column reflectors -> compact H,tau) = 24838 (4.7x); fusing the trailing sub into baddbmm + replacing the O(r) larft loop with closed-form T=inv(triu(VtV,1)+diag(1/tau)) via one solve_triangular = 8038 (14.6x, killed thousands of tiny launches); per-n panel width (R={512:64,1024:32,2048:16,...}, the panel tile must shrink as n grows or it spills) + geqrf-panel for n=4096 (B=2 starves one-CTA-per-matrix; cuSOLVER spreads the tall-skinny panel over many CTAs) = 5974 (19.7x); bf16x3 split GEMM (Ah@Bh+Ah@Bl+Al@Bh, fp32 accum, ~5e-6 rel) for the n>=2048 trailing updates = 5878. WHAT DIDNT WORK: tf32 trailing fails ill-conditioned large-n gates; single-pass fp16/bf16 trailing fails the n=512 rowscale gate; bf16x3 is only faster than fp32 cuBLAS when M,N,K are all large (the QR trailing GEMMs are skinny, K=panel width), so it is a wash/loss at n<=1024. KEY REMAINING BOTTLENECK: the panel kernel is 46% of the dominant B=640 n=512 shape and ~73% of n=4096, and is capped by the sm_120 100KB SRAM wall (this is the workstation RTX PRO 6000, NOT 228KB B200) + the sequential per-column BLAS-2 recurrence -- R=64 at n=512 already spills. A recursive in-kernel panel (tl.dot WY apply) and bf16 panel storage both hit the SRAM wall / accuracy wall. NEXT BRIEF IDEA: a COOPERATIVE multi-CTA panel (several CTAs per matrix tiling the m rows, grid-sync or two-phase global reduction between the norm and the apply) to fix both the SRAM cap and the tiny-batch occupancy starvation -- that is the one thing that can beat cuSOLVER's panel and unlock the next 2x. The trailing GEMMs (42% at n=512) are a secondary target only once the panel is fixed.

TSQR / communication-avoiding panel factorization to break the panel kernel that is now your bottleneck (46% of n=512, 73% of n=4096), fixing all three pains you profiled: the 100KB SRAM wall, the sequential per-column BLAS-2 recurrence, and one-CTA-per-matrix occupancy starvation at n=4096 B=2. Partition the m panel rows into independent row-tiles; each CTA factors its small tile with ZERO cross-CTA sync (sidestepping Triton 3.6's lack of grid.sync), then a log-depth reduction tree merges the per-tile R factors (expressible as 2-3 hazard-free producer/consumer launches: leaf-factor, then tree-merge). Reconstruct compact (H,tau) from the TSQR factors so the geqrf contract + tight factor/orth gates hold on ill-conditioned shapes. Keep fp32 (mixed precision is your already-explored lane); off-grid n routes to geqrf. Targets tall n=2048/4096 and the dominant n=512.

Evaluated TSQR/TSQR-HR panel end-to-end (Triton row-tiled leaf + merge + form-Q + Modified-LU Householder reconstruction, all-Triton/bmm to dodge cuSOLVER's looping batched QR/orgqr). CORRECT (recon ~1e-5, orth ~1e-6 incl ill-conditioned) but 4-9x SLOWER than the single-launch panel: n=512 0.25x, n=2048 0.13x, n=4096 0.11x. Root cause: single-GPU panel wants FEWER launches not more (TSQR's gain is distributed-mem sync); the Householder reconstruction dominates and its Modified-LU needs the full mxR Q resident -> SAME ~100KB SRAM wall it was meant to dodge (only MOVES the wall). Triton leaf factor alone IS fast (183us/2560 tiles, fixes occupancy) -- it's the reconstruction that kills it. Kept the 20x best unchanged. geomean 5926 (20.0x).

TSQR / TSQR-HR panel: built end-to-end, proven correct, measured DECISIVELY SLOWER (4-9x) -- a clean negative result. Best stays the brief-0 kernel, geomean ~5926 us = 20.0x (HEAD b71e459, validates clean, all guards). WHAT I DID: full all-Triton/bmm TSQR-HR avoiding cuSOLVER's looping batched QR/orgqr -- row-tiled Triton leaf factor (1 launch) + R-factor merge + form orthonormal Q via bmm + Householder reconstruction via Modified-LU of (Q - sign-diag). Verified correct: recon ~1e-5, orth ~1e-6 incl ill-conditioned rankdef/clustered/nearrank/upper. RESULT: full-QR was n=512 0.25x, n=2048 0.13x, n=4096 0.11x of current. ROOT CAUSE (the important takeaway): (1) On a single GPU the panel wants FEWER kernel launches, not more -- TSQR's win is distributed-memory synchronization avoidance, which doesn't exist here; my current panel is ONE launch for the whole panel, TSQR-HR is ~10+ launches (leaf, T-solves, Q-bmms, merge, combine, R-iteration Modified-LU, reconstruct). (2) DECISIVELY: the Householder reconstruction's Modified-LU needs the full m x R Q factor resident, so it hits the EXACT SAME ~100KB sm_120 SRAM wall TSQR was meant to dodge -- TSQR only MOVES the wall from the factorization to the reconstruction, it doesn't remove it. The cuSOLVER batched QR/orgqr routines also loop (orgqr on 2560 tiles = 100ms), so any PyTorch-level TSQR is hopeless. SALVAGEABLE POSITIVE: the Triton row-tiled LEAF factor alone is fast (183us for 2560 tiles, fixes occupancy) -- it's purely the reconstruction that kills it. CONCLUSION: the panel bottleneck (46% n=512, 73% n=4096) is fundamental to single-GPU batched compact-Householder QR on a 100KB-SRAM part; neither grid-sync (Triton lacks it) nor TSQR-HR (SRAM wall + launch overhead) beats the single-launch panel + per-shape method (Triton wide-batch / geqrf tiny-batch). I recommend AGAINST further panel-restructuring briefs. Higher-EV next directions instead: (a) attack the 42% trailing GEMMs at n=512 with a single FUSED Triton kernel for V^T@A + T^T@(.) + V@W (cut the 3 cuBLAS launches + intermediates to one), (b) cut the form_T trsm (4.7%) and the V-extraction triu_tril (2.7%) by fusing V/T construction into the panel kernel's epilogue, (c) overlap panel(k+1) leaf with trailing-update(k) since they're independent once V_k is known.

Fuse the trailing-update GEMM chain (now ~42% of n=512 after the panel is squeezed). Collapse the three trailing matmuls V^T@A -> W=T^T@(.) -> A-=V@W into ONE Triton kernel that keeps the W intermediate in SRAM/registers instead of round-tripping HBM, cutting both launch count and the n*W intermediate traffic. Also fold the V-extraction (triu/tril split, 2.7%) and form_T (trsm, 4.7%) into the panel kernel's epilogue so per-panel launches drop further. Optionally overlap panel(k+1)'s leaf factor with trailing-update(k) (independent once V_k is known). Keep fp32 (mixed precision is your mapped dead-end); compact (H,tau); off-grid n -> geqrf. Targets the dominant B=640 n=512 and B=60 n=1024.

Fused trailing-update chain (V^T@A -> T^T@(.) -> A-=V@W) into ONE Triton kernel: each program owns a col-block (all M rows), reduces V^T@A over row-tiles with V resident, keeps W in registers (no HBM round-trip), applies in a 2nd pass. tl.dot input_precision=ieee -> bit-identical to fp32 cuBLAS, 1.3x faster in isolation. Used for fp32 shapes n=176..1024. Validates clean incl all guards. geomean 5647 = 1.04x vs prev, 20.8x vs baseline. n=1024 10.5->9.2ms. (Note: 'stream' substring anywhere in submission.py triggers the leaderboard banned-construct rejection.)

Read V implicitly from H in the fused trailing kernel + a new Gram (V^T V) kernel, both applying the unit-lower mask in registers. Eliminates the materialized V tensor, both triu/tril kernels, the diagonal index-set, and the cuBLAS V^T V bmm for the fp32 'fused' shapes (folds brief part 2). Bit-identical (ieee tl.dot). Validates clean incl all guards. geomean 5086 = 1.11x vs prev, 23.1x vs baseline. n=176 1.5x, n=512 1.13x, n=1024 1.15x.

Folded form_T into a fused Gram+T kernel (reads V implicit, forms G in SRAM, fills T by in-kernel larft recurrence) for narrow panels R<=32; R-dispatched (R=64 keeps Gram kernel + cuBLAS trsm since the sequential recurrence loses for wide R). Bit-identical (rel ~1e-8 on real geqrf data). Validates clean incl all guards. geomean 4704 = 1.08x vs iter2, 25.0x vs baseline. n=176 1.4x, n=1024 1.13x, n=512 held.
Tuned fused-trailing BN/BM/num_warps by panel width (R<=32: BN32/BM64/8warps; R=64: BN64/BM16/4warps). geomean 4651 = 1.01x vs prev, 25.3x vs baseline. Validates clean.

Parametrized fused trailing kernel with a BF16 flag (big V^T@A,V@W via bf16x3 tensor cores ~5e-6 rel; T^T@VtA stays fp32). n=2048 switched to 'fused_bf16' (implicit-V fused Gram+T + fused bf16x3 trailing) = 2.05x on that shape (26.2->12.8ms). n=4096 keeps explicit-V bf16 (R=256 exceeds fused kernels' ~100KB SRAM). Validates clean incl ill-conditioned gates. geomean 4457 = 1.04x vs prev, 26.4x vs baseline.

Re-swept panel width post-fusion: R=32 now beats R=64 for n=352/512 (R=32 panel fits SRAM without spilling + uses fully-fused Gram+T dropping cuBLAS trsm; cheaper fused trailing pays for extra panels). geomean 3999 = 1.11x vs prev, 29.4x vs baseline. n=512 11.6->9.4ms (1.24x), n=352 1.5->0.82ms (1.84x). Validates clean.

Fused trailing-update chain: STRONG SUCCESS. geomean 5928 -> 4000 us = 1.48x on this brief, 29.4x over the 117536 baseline (HEAD 79b357f, validates clean, all guards incl ill-conditioned). Iterations: (1) collapsed V^T@A->T^T@(.)->A-=V@W into ONE Triton kernel keeping W in registers (no HBM round-trip), tl.dot input_precision=ieee -> bit-identical fp32, 1.3x in isolation; (2) read V IMPLICITLY from H in the trailing + a Gram kernel (V^T V) -- dropped the materialized V tensor, both triu/tril, the diagonal index-set, and the cuBLAS V^T V bmm (brief part 2) = 23.1x; (3) folded form_T into a fused Gram+T kernel (in-kernel larft recurrence) for R<=32, R-dispatched (R=64 keeps cuBLAS trsm) = 25.0x; (4) bf16-flag on the fused trailing -> 'fused_bf16' for n=2048 = 2.05x on that shape (26.2->12.8ms) = 26.4x; (5) RE-SWEPT panel width post-fusion: R=32 now beats R=64 at n=352/512 (R=32 fits SRAM unspilled + uses fully-fused Gram+T, and the now-cheap fused trailing pays for extra panels) = 29.4x (n=512 1.24x, n=352 1.84x). PROFILE shift: n=512 panel dropped 52%->29%, trailing is now THE bottleneck (61% at both n=512 and n=1024), all cuBLAS glue gone. WHAT DIDNT WORK / dead ends mapped: part 3 (overlap panel(k+1) with trailing(k)) is BLOCKED -- CUDA streams are banned by the leaderboard scan, no multi-stream possible. A 2-level QR (narrow R=32 inner panel + wide-K outer trailing) to raise the memory-bound K=32 trailing's arithmetic intensity is BLOCKED by the same ~100KB SRAM wall: R_outer>64 OOMs the Gram/trailing kernels, and R_outer=64 gives no win. The fp32 fused trailing at K=32 is memory-bound (intensity ~32 FLOP/elem vs ~117 crossover) but cannot get wider K without spilling. bf16x3 doesn't help the fp32 shapes (K=32 too skinny, same memory traffic + more compute). REMAINING: the trailing (61%) is near its floor given SRAM; the panel (29%) is fundamental (brief-1 proved). I'd judge the kernel near speed-of-light for this hardware/algorithm. CAUTION for future: any 'stream' substring in submission.py (even a comment) triggers the leaderboard banned-construct rejection -- the validate scan caught it once. Possible micro next: n=4096 (52ms, the largest single shape) still uses the OLD explicit-V bf16 path because its R=256 geqrf panel exceeds the fused kernels' SRAM; a custom large-R trailing that tiles R could shave it, but it's 1 of 12 shapes.

COMBINE for the biggest remaining lever: large-n. By marginal log-analysis the geomean is now dragged by n=2048 (~1.1x) and n=4096 (~1x, still pure geqrf) while everything else is 25-60x - lifting n=4096 even to ~10x is worth more than any n<=1024 tweak. Worker 1 proved large-n is PANEL-FACTORIZATION-bound (~83% geqrf panel). You own BOTH ingredients: your brief-1 TSQR row-tiled LEAF factor (b71e4597 - fast, 183us/2560 tiles, fixes the tall-skinny low-batch occupancy starvation that one-CTA-per-matrix hits at n=4096 B=2) AND your brief-2 fused trailing + closed-form/Gram-T leader (79b357ff, 29.4x). Stack them: use the TSQR-style row-tiled panel factor for the n>=2048 panel (replacing geqrf's geqr2_smem_domino panel), feed its V/tau into your fused multi-CTA trailing update. The TSQR reconstruction overhead that killed it standalone is moot here - you're using the LEAF FACTOR for speed, not the HR reconstruction. Keep compact (H,tau), fp32, hold gates on ill-cond. n<=1024 keeps your current 29.4x path; only n>=2048 changes. NO cuda streams (banned). Target n=2048 and n=4096.

COMBINE (TSQR leaf for n>=2048 panel) evaluated end-to-end -- quantified DEAD END. n=2048 (B=8): my single-CTA Triton panel R=16 is ~50us/panel (spill cheap at R=16) vs geqrf ~590us vs TSQR ~350us -- Triton wins, n=2048 unchanged (already 5x faster than worker1's geqrf-hybrid). n=4096 (B=2): panel-bound ~82% geqr2; TSQR-HR panel ~26x SLOWER than geqrf (Modified-LU reconstruct alone 3.2ms > geqrf's whole 0.86ms panel; Q-formation 19ms dwarfs both); geqrf-wide-panel+bounded-fused-sub-block trailing also slower (59-65 vs 52ms: R=64 sub-blocks = N/64 trailing passes vs geqrf-R256 single K=256 pass). Worker 1 independently kept geqrf for n=4096. Kept kernel unchanged (doc comment only). geomean 3997 (29.4x), validates clean.

COMBINE (TSQR leaf x fused trailing for large-n): thorough QUANTIFIED NEGATIVE result. Best stays the brief-2 fused-trailing kernel, geomean 3997 us = 29.4x (HEAD b149b8c, validates clean, all guards; kernel byte-identical to brief-2's 79b357ff, only a documenting comment added). The combine cannot improve either large-n shape, for measured reasons:

n=2048 (B=8): NOT a TSQR opportunity. My single-CTA Triton panel at R=16 factors each panel in ~50us (its 128KB tile nominally spills to local but that is cheap at R=16) -- vs geqrf ~590us and a TSQR leaf+merge+formQ ~350us. So my current path (Triton panel R=16 + fused_bf16 trailing, 12.8ms) is already optimal and ~5x faster than worker 1's geqrf-hybrid (67.9ms) on this shape. Panel is only 33% there; trailing 51% is the (already-fused-bf16) bottleneck.

n=4096 (B=2): genuinely panel-bound (~82% geqrf geqr2_gmem/smem_domino) but geqrf IS the floor. (1) A row-tiled TSQR-HR panel is ~26x SLOWER than geqrf: the Householder reconstruction's Modified-LU ALONE (~3.2ms) exceeds geqrf's entire panel factorization (~0.86ms), and the Q-formation (~19ms) dwarfs both -- the reconstruction overhead is fundamentally larger than what it replaces (this re-confirms my brief-1 finding with a sharper single-panel measurement). (2) My single-CTA Triton panel truly starves at B=2 (R=16 spills to ~163ms). (3) geqrf-wide-panel(R=256) + bounded fused sub-block(R=64) trailing is also slower (59-65ms vs 52ms) because R=64 sub-blocks make N/64 sequential trailing passes vs geqrf-R256's single high-arithmetic-intensity K=256 pass. Worker 1 independently reached the same conclusion and KEPT geqrf for n=4096.

The TSQR leaf's only genuine strength (cheap row-tiled occupancy fix) is moot here: where occupancy is a problem (n=4096 B=2) the reconstruction overhead overwhelms the gain, and where it would be cheap (n=2048 B=8) my single-CTA panel already wins. The leaf factor was the salvageable brief-1 positive, but the combine confirms it cannot be assembled into a geqrf-beating panel for the compact-(H,tau) contract on this 100KB-SRAM part. RECOMMENDATION: stop large-n panel restructuring -- the panel floor is geqrf (n=4096) / my Triton kernel (n=2048), both proven. The only remaining frontier to #1 (~1293us, mxfp10 per worker 2) is extreme low precision, which is outside this run's fp32 constraint. I judge my 29.4x kernel at the fp32 speed-of-light for this hardware.

Holistic LAUNCH-COUNT reduction on the 32.8x leader - the precision frontier is closed (bf16x3 optimal on sm_120; 1293us is B200-only), so remaining wins are structural, and launch/python-dispatch overhead is the untapped one. The small/mid shapes (n=32 b=20, n=176 b=40, n=352 b=40) are almost certainly launch-overhead-bound not compute-bound: at n=32 the GPU work is trivial yet you pay per-launch dispatch across n/W super-panels x (panel-factor + Gram+T + trailing) kernels. Collapse per-super-panel launches into one mega-launch where the ~100KB smem permits (generous at small n), hoist invariant python-side setup out of the per-panel loop, and batch/fuse torch-level ops to cut python dispatch. You own this kernel's launch structure - it's your turf. NO cuda streams (banned, even in comments). Stay OFF worker 1's hot n<=1024 fused-combine MATH (it's actively improving that); you're attacking launch COUNT/overhead, a distinct axis. Keep compact (H,tau), fp32, hold all gates. Target the small/mid shapes + any per-launch savings that also help n=512/1024.

Validates clean.

Launch-count reduction: SOLID WIN. geomean 3659 -> ~3150-3225 us = ~1.14-1.16x on this brief (HEAD a4d9a6e, validates clean, all guards), on top of worker 1's 32.8x combine. Three launch/dispatch-overhead wins, all bit-identical, no touch to worker 1's trailing/T ALGEBRA:
(1) FUSED panel-factor + compact-WY T into ONE kernel (_panel_factor_T) for n<=352 -- saves the separate Gram+T launch per panel; dispatched only for the launch-bound small/mid shapes (n>=512 measured 0.98x with it: the extra serial T-build in the panel's critical path costs more than the launch saved there).
(2) PER-PANEL num_warps auto-selected from BLOCK_M (a pure launch/occupancy knob, swept: <=64->1, 128->2, 256/512->4, 1024->8, >=2048->16; pf_T wants more: <=256->4 else 8) replacing the fixed nw=8. (3) Cut per-call python/launch overhead: torch.empty TAU instead of torch.zeros (the panels write every column, so the zero-fill launch was pure waste -- helps EVERY shape), and lazy arange (only the explicit-V _form_T path builds it). n=32 -> 16.6us (2.1x total from baseline 35.6).
Per-shape final: n=32 16.6us (2.1x), n=176 236us (1.2x), n=352 645us (1.13x), n=512 ~7200us (1.13x), n=1024 ~6200us, n=2048 ~12.1ms, n=4096 ~50ms.
WHERE IT ENDS: the small/mid shapes are now PANEL-COMPUTE-bound not launch-bound (n=176 profile: pf_T 77%, trailing 19% -- 2 launches/panel is the floor without grid-sync, which is banned/unavailable). n=512+ are trailing-compute-bound (n=512: trailing 70%, panel 22%). NOTE: run-to-run variance is ~2-5% on the larger shapes (GPU scheduling/thermal on the shared host); the small-shape wins are stable. I judge the launch-count axis exhausted; remaining headroom is in the panel-factor compute (worker 1's lane) or closed (precision frontier per worker 2).
